column1: # host-posture.tsv — THE SINGLE PLACE A MACHINE'S SERVICE-STATE POSTURE IS DECIDED
# THIS FILE IS THE AUTHORITY FOR `scripts/mesh/guard-service-state.sh`.
# The guard reads the designation from HERE, never from a hardcoded list, so the
# next cutover (or the next freeze) only has to update this one file.
# FORMAT — one host per line, FIVE fields separated by a PIPE `|` (not whitespace:
# whitespace does not survive an editor and a lost tab silently moves every field):
#   1  host      the hostname, or ANY ssh alias / tailnet name that resolves to it.
#                An agent may arrive as `secratary`, `secratary-ts`, `secratary-lan`
#                or `192.168.50.77`; every one of those names must be present.
#   2  posture   one of:  frozen | read-only | writable
#                  frozen    — service state is FROZEN BY DECISION. Do not start,
#                              stop, mask, unmask, enable, disable or restart
#                              anything. A masked unit on a frozen host is
#                              DELIBERATE. Refused.
#                  read-only — the tree/database is not to be written, and service
#                              state is refused unless --owner-confirmed.
#                  writable  — normal host; service changes permitted.
#   3  since     ISO-8601 UTC of the decision (why the state looks as it does).
#   4  decided   who or what decided it, and where the decision is written down.
#   5  reason    one plain-language sentence. This is the text an agent reads when
#                the guard refuses it, so it must say WHY, not just WHAT.
# Lines beginning with `#` and blank lines are ignored. The header line below is a
# comment, deliberately, so a blank or dotted column can never parse as a posture.
# host | posture | since | decided | reason
